-17.4 % QoQIn Q1 26, shrimp feed sales remained high at THB 880mn, increasing 
13.1% YoY. The increase was mainly driven by significant volume growth of 
16.0% YoY , supported by the following: 
• Thailand: Performance was supported by stronger domestic demand 
from key customers nationwide with ongoing market share gains. 
• Indonesia: Shrimp feed sales declined 20.4% YoY amid intense 
competition and lower shrimp stocking activity, while the Company 
continued to strengthen its technical support capabilities.
• GPM dropped by 0.8% YoY to 21.9%  driven mainly by higher fishmeal 
prices offset by higher sales volume.

-19.0%  QoQIn Q1 26, fish feed sales were broadly flat at THB 356mn YoY  with sales 
volume down 0.5%. Seabass feed volumes fell amid heightened 
competition. Volumes of other fish feed also declined; however, sales value 
increased due to a shift in product mix, driven by diversification into 
species such as tilapia, snakehead fish, gourami, and catfish. This growth 
was partly offset by weak tilapia prices, which prompted farmers to switch 
to lower -priced feed, as well as reduced gourami farming activity following 
lingering pandemic effects.
GPM also dropped by 5.7% YoY to 16.8% in Q4 25 , driven mainly by higher 
fishmeal prices.

-28.0%  QoQIn Q1 26, Livestock feed sales declined by 17.4% YoY , reflecting 
challenging industry conditions marked by lower livestock prices and 
reduced farming activity. Sales were further impacted by portfolio 
optimization initiatives —including SKU rationalization, customer base 
streamlining in Thailand, and the exit from Pakistan in 2025 —as the 
Company focuses on higher -margin, more profitable products. The 
market situation is expected to gradually improve, leading to more 
farming activities, while the Company is focusing on feed quality 
consistency and supporting services to gain more market share. 
GPM stood at 14.7% in Q1 26. improving from 13.5% in Q1 25 and from 
10.2% in Q4 25.

2026 Guidance Key drivers
Sales growth + 8 – 10% YoY •TFM’s sales are expected to grow by 8 – 10% YoY , 
mainly driven by continued strong momentum in 
shrimp feed and fish feed in Thailand.
GPM 18 – 20% • GPM is expected to remain at a high level, supported 
by consistently strong production yields, a healthy 
product -mix profile, optimized product costs, and 
effective raw -material cost management.
SG&A to sales 8 – 10% • SG&A to sales implemented additional cost -saving 
initiatives to balance the increased sales and 
marketing efforts needed to support further growth. 
CAPEX THB 680mn • A significant portion is allocated to the new plant in
